study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition (EPIC)
reason: The abstract evaluates incident prostate cancer overall. It mentions subgroup analyses by stage or grade but does not explicitly identify an advanced, high-grade, high-risk, metastatic, lethal, or otherwise aggressive incident endpoint or define the stage/grade categories.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: No significant association was found between 25-hydroxyvitamin D and risk of prostate cancer (highest vs. lowest quintile: odds ratio = 1.28, 95% confidence interval: 0.88, 1.88; P for trend = 0.188).
estimate_classifications.reason: The estimate is explicitly for overall prostate cancer risk, not an aggressive subtype.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
